title: The Open Ledger
intro: Lorn's council has announced that the evacuation is complete. Mara Rook can still hear people behind the gate. The dead at the wheel are obeying an old instruction, and eleven bells repeat it across the city. A twelfth bell has no name. Enter the cordon, find the people the ledger left out, and decide what the city should remember.

acts.title: A way inside
acts.speaker: Mara Rook
acts.text: The first task is small enough to say aloud: open a door and bring someone through it. The gate will lead to a ward, a workshop and a list. The order in which we reach them matters.

acts.title: The work of the living
acts.speaker: Tamsin Reed
acts.text: The city still works. Ovens burn, clocks turn and pumps empty the river into the streets. Their operators are dead. Somewhere a command is being copied faster than we can break it.

acts.title: Everyone has a name
acts.speaker: Sable Quill
acts.text: The council's final bell does not command the dead to rise. It tells them whom to ignore. We have followed the order to its source. Now we must choose what will replace it.

beats.title: The hinge
beats.speaker: Mara Rook
beats.text: The gate stops repeating its lock order. Beneath the wheel we find a brass plate: EVACUATION COMPLETE. Fresh chalk names cover the wall below it. Someone inside the cordon has been keeping a different account.

choices.title: Bring out the families
choices.text: Make room for the people waiting at the triage passage.

choices.title: Copy the chalk names
choices.text: Take a witness list through the old registry gate.

choices.title: Cut the alarm wire
choices.text: Break the signal that keeps the workshops sealed.

beats.title: Three addresses
beats.speaker: Iona Vale
beats.text: A porter gives us three addresses and only one unbroken handcart. One holds patients, one holds their admission slips, and one holds the mechanism that marks the slips refused. We cannot be everywhere at once.

choices.title: Take the cart to the ward
choices.text: Carry blankets and drinking water toward the infirmary.

choices.title: Recover the admission slips
choices.text: Keep proof of who was turned away.

choices.title: Stop the refusal machine
choices.text: Remove the seal before more doors obey it.

beats.title: The red door
beats.speaker: Bram Voss
beats.text: The door is painted red on both sides. The people behind it were told that red meant safety; the watch were told that it meant infection. Bram takes the handle off and carries it with him. There will be no second locking.

choices.title: Escort the people inside
choices.text: Give the slowest walkers a protected route.

choices.title: Find the watch order
choices.text: Read the original instruction rather than another copy.

choices.title: Break the locking gear
choices.text: Make the next red door impossible to close.

beats.title: The measure
beats.speaker: Sable Quill
beats.text: The council called its sorting device a diagnostic instrument. Its scales have no weight marks, only columns for accepted and unlisted. The glass is cracked from the inside. Someone tried to make the result come out differently.

choices.title: Treat the unlisted
choices.text: Take the rejected patients somewhere a form cannot stop them.

choices.title: Keep the broken measure
choices.text: Carry the instrument as evidence of what it was built to do.

choices.title: Destroy the stencil
choices.text: Stop the workshops making another identical scale.

beats.title: No one left outside
beats.speaker: Mara Rook
beats.text: The next cart reaches the gate without an admission stamp. Nothing terrible happens. A child asks why everyone looks surprised. Beyond the wall, the bells begin the next shift. We have opened one door; the city can still close a thousand.

choices.title: Shelter the first convoy
choices.text: Prepare a quiet place for the next group to arrive.

choices.title: Deliver the witness list
choices.text: Let the outer watch see whose names were missing.

choices.title: Follow the shift signal
choices.text: Trace the order back through the working machinery.

beats.title: The bread line
beats.speaker: Hux Bell
beats.text: The ovens are full, but the queue is empty. Hux finds a week's wages tied into a baker's apron. The flour has been counted as fuel. He remembers working hungry beside this furnace, when the bells still called it a privilege.

choices.title: Send the flour to the ward
choices.text: Turn a counted resource into something people can eat.

choices.title: Record the unpaid names
choices.text: Carry the workers' accounts out of the furnace hall.

choices.title: Pull the coal chain
choices.text: Stop the next shift before the furnace can demand it.

beats.title: Unpaid hours
beats.speaker: Tamsin Reed
beats.text: Every clock has kept the same minute. Each time its hand reaches the next mark, a ratchet pulls it back. Tamsin could repair the ratchet with her eyes closed. Instead she asks who benefits from a shift that cannot end.

choices.title: Give the crews a rest
choices.text: Move the trapped workers toward the infirmary courtyard.

choices.title: Take the time sheets
choices.text: Preserve the hours that the clocks refused to finish.

choices.title: Remove the ratchet
choices.text: Let the machines reach tomorrow without another command.

beats.title: The flooded register
beats.speaker: Vale Ash
beats.text: The post bag is too heavy to lift until the water drains from it. Each letter begins with the same apology for being late. Vale finds one addressed to a person who has been helping us since the gate. Nobody has told them the letter arrived.

choices.title: Ferry the waiting families
choices.text: Use the chapel steps as a dry gathering place.

choices.title: Deliver every letter
choices.text: Bring the bag to the registry and find its living addresses.

choices.title: Open the flood controls
choices.text: Cut the command that keeps the streets under water.

beats.title: A reason to sing
beats.speaker: Sable Quill
beats.text: The choir's score has no words. Its rests are marked with tiny names, crossed out one by one. When Sable reads a name into the silence, someone on the far side of the room answers. The bells hesitate for a single beat.

choices.title: Keep a quiet room
choices.text: Make space for the voices that are still frightened to answer.

choices.title: Carry the marked score
choices.text: Keep the erased names beside the witnesses who know them.

choices.title: Disconnect the amplifier
choices.text: Stop the order being made louder than a human voice.

beats.title: The city answers
beats.speaker: Mara Rook
beats.text: Three districts answer the radio without giving a registration number. The council replies that this is impossible: its ledger has no empty beds, no unpaid hours and no undelivered post. Then a second voice whispers a question beneath the official broadcast. How many names have we found?

choices.title: Keep the convoys moving
choices.text: Let the answer be the people arriving outside the cordon.

choices.title: Bring the ledger to council
choices.text: Place the witnesses beside the account that erased them.

choices.title: Sever the broadcast line
choices.text: Find the machinery that keeps speaking over the second voice.

beats.title: One blank column
beats.speaker: Iona Vale
beats.text: The blank column is not a space for people whose names were lost. It is a place for people the council decided not to name. Iona reads the small print twice. There was always room in the infirmary; the empty beds were being held for better entries.

choices.title: Give the beds to the living
choices.text: Finish the evacuation before arguing with another form.

choices.title: Trace every blank entry
choices.text: Ask each witness who should have occupied the missing line.

choices.title: Break the reservation seals
choices.text: Prevent the blank column being used again.

beats.title: The procession
beats.speaker: Bram Voss
beats.text: The procession carries empty boxes beneath the city banners. Bram recognizes the step: he once marched it at the head of an evacuation. Nobody is leading this one. The order has outlived everyone who could remember where it was meant to go.

choices.title: Build a living corridor
choices.text: Hold a route for people who can choose their destination.

choices.title: Identify the bearers
choices.text: Give the procession back the names its banners concealed.

choices.title: Lower the city standard
choices.text: End the march instead of finding another leader for it.

beats.title: A bell without a rope
beats.speaker: Tamsin Reed
beats.text: The twelfth bell has no rope and no clapper. It rings when the other eleven agree that somebody does not count. Tamsin lays a hand against its housing and feels the metal hesitate. A machine can repeat an order. It cannot decide whom we owe an answer.

choices.title: Protect the last carriers
choices.text: Make sure the witnesses reach the end of the route alive.

choices.title: Read the missing names
choices.text: Carry the second account into the council chamber.

choices.title: Remove the governor
choices.text: Keep the bells from being forced into agreement again.

beats.title: The last order
beats.speaker: Mara Rook
beats.text: The council offers to open the cordon if we certify its original evacuation as complete. Nobody has to change a name; we only have to stop counting. Mara leaves the form unsigned. The last order is already coming down the wire. Choose what we will hold when it arrives.

choices.title: Hold the evacuation corridor
choices.text: Put the people coming home before any signature.

choices.title: Answer with the complete list
choices.text: Bring every recovered name into the final hearing.

choices.title: Refuse the command
choices.text: Disconnect the authority that can issue another order.

beats.title: The account remains open
beats.speaker: Mara Rook
beats.text: The last order ends before its final word. Across Lorn, doors remain open without waiting for another instruction. We cannot bring back everyone the city lost. We can decide what it means to keep their place.

endings.title: A road stays open
endings.speaker: Iona Vale
endings.text: The ward runs out of forms before it runs out of beds. Iona uses the clean backs of the pages to write directions to the gate. Every convoy leaves room for somebody who walks slowly. On the first morning without an order, Mara asks whether they should close the cordon. Nobody can think of a reason. The city will remember the missing by making space for whoever arrives next.

endings.title: Names answered
endings.speaker: Vale Ash
endings.text: They put two ledgers on the council table. One says the evacuation was complete. The other contains handwriting from every district: a cook's mark, a child's drawing, names somebody remembered while carrying a stretcher. Vale leaves the last page blank and places a pencil beside it. Every evening the witnesses read what has been added. The twelfth bell is quiet while somebody is answering.

endings.title: No order after this
endings.speaker: Tamsin Reed
endings.text: Tamsin removes the governor without replacing it. The eleven bells can sound the hours, but none can command a door to close. Hux asks how the next shift will know when to begin. People can ask each other, she says. Beyond the foundry, one surviving wire trembles against the stones. They leave it there as a reminder: a city should never be so well ordered that nobody can refuse it.
